title: Receiving Tips from Clients Standard
summary: Tips are accepted as a voluntary gesture of appreciation and placed into a general tip account for fairness and transparency. Therapists must never request, demand, suggest, or pressure a client for a tip.

sections.title: The Standard
paragraphs: At Zura Spa, we accept tips from clients as a gesture of appreciation for good service. However, all tips received from clients are placed into a general tip account for fairness, transparency, and uniformity among the team.

Tips are therefore not treated as the personal entitlement of an individual therapist. The general tip arrangement allows the team to benefit fairly while maintaining a consistent and professional system.
Most importantly, therapists must never request, demand, suggest, or pressure a client for a tip. A tip should always be given voluntarily by the client.

sections.title: Relevance of the Standard
paragraphs: This standard is important because it:
list: Promotes fairness and uniformity among therapists.
Prevents competition between therapists over tips.
Protects clients from feeling pressured or obligated to tip.
Maintains professional boundaries between therapists and clients.
Prevents misunderstandings and disputes concerning money.
Encourages therapists to focus on quality service rather than personal financial gain.
Protects the reputation and professionalism of Zura Spa.
Creates a transparent system that benefits the team as a whole.

sections.title: Therapist's Mindset Towards Tips
paragraphs: Therapists should understand that a tip is a client's voluntary expression of appreciation, not something they are owed or should expect.
The right mindset is: "My responsibility is to give the best service I can. If a client chooses to appreciate the service with a tip, I receive it respectfully and follow the Zura Spa tip standard."

Therapists should never measure the quality of their service by the amount of tips they receive. The primary goal should always be client satisfaction, professionalism, and delivering the Zura Spa experience.
A therapist should also understand that accepting a tip through the general account is an act of teamwork and fairness, not a loss of personal entitlement.

sections.title: What Therapists Should Do
list: Accept tips graciously when a client voluntarily offers one.
Thank the client politely for their generosity.
Ensure the tip is submitted through the approved general tip account/system.
Follow management's procedure for recording or submitting tips.
Maintain professionalism regardless of whether a client tips or does not tip.
Treat every client with the same level of care and attention.
Report any questions or concerns about the tip system to management.

sections.title: What Therapists Should Not Do
list: Do not ask a client for a tip.
Do not hint or make comments intended to make a client feel obligated to tip.
Do not negotiate with a client about the amount of a tip.
Do not compare your tips with those of other therapists.
Do not hide or privately keep a tip that is required to go into the general account.
Do not treat clients differently because they did not give a tip.
Do not discuss tips with clients in a way that creates pressure or discomfort.
Do not argue with a colleague over who deserves a particular tip.
Do not allow personal expectations about tips to affect the quality of your service.

sections.title: Zura Spa Mindset
paragraphs: We serve first. We appreciate voluntarily given tips. We do not request them. We share through the agreed system.
At Zura Spa, the quality of our service should never depend on whether a client gives a tip. Every client deserves the same professionalism, care, respect, and exceptional service.
A tip is appreciation, not an expectation. Our standard is to serve excellently, regardless of whether we are appreciated or not.

remember: A tip is appreciation, not an expectation. Serve excellently — never request, demand, or pressure a client for a tip.
